practice.prompt: Triangle ABC has AB=AC and each base angle is 48°. Find vertex angle A.
practice.solution: Because AB=AC, angles B and C each equal 48°. Angle A=180−48−48=84°.

practice.prompt: An isosceles triangle has a 40° vertex angle. Find each base angle.
practice.solution: The two equal base angles share 180−40=140°, so each is 140/2=70°.

practice.prompt: Triangle ABC has AB=AC and angle B=65°. Find angle C.
practice.solution: Equal sides AB and AC are opposite angles C and B. Therefore angle C equals angle B, or 65°.

practice.prompt: Two base angles in an isosceles triangle each measure 32°. Find the vertex angle.
practice.solution: Vertex=180−2(32)=116°, since the three interior angles total 180°.

practice.prompt: An isosceles triangle has a 96° vertex angle. Find a base angle.
practice.solution: Subtract 96 from 180 and divide the remaining 84° equally: 42°.

practice.prompt: The vertex angle is (3x+18)° and each base angle is (x+21)°. Find x.
The base angles are (2x+9)° and (5x−36)°. Find x.
practice.solution: Equal base angles give 2x+9=5x−36; therefore 45=3x and x=15.

practice.prompt: Equal sides are 13 cm each, and the base is 10 cm. Find the perimeter in cm.
practice.solution: The perimeter is the sum of all sides: 13+13+10=36 cm.

practice.prompt: The perimeter is 50 cm and the base is 14 cm. Find the length of either equal side.
practice.solution: Remove the base: 50−14=36 cm. Divide the remaining length by two equal sides: 18 cm.

practice.prompt: The two base angles are (5x−12)° and (3x+18)°. Find x.
practice.solution: Set 5x−12=3x+18. Subtract 3x and add 12: 2x=30, so x=15.

practice.prompt: The vertex is (2x+28)° and each base angle is (3x−4)°. Find x.
Can lengths 9, 9, and 19 form an isosceles triangle? Answer Yes or No.
practice.solution: No: the triangle inequality fails because 9+9=18 is less than 19.

practice.prompt: Each base angle is 72°. Find the exterior angle at the vertex.
practice.solution: The interior vertex is 180−144=36°. Its adjacent exterior is 180−36=144°.

practice.prompt: The base angles are (x+24)° and (3x−16)°. Find the vertex angle.
practice.solution: Set x+24=3x−16, giving x=20. Each base angle is 44°, so vertex=180−88=92°.

practice.prompt: The vertex angle is (5x+10)° and each base angle is (2x+4)°. Find x.
Triangle ABC has AB=AC. Exterior angle at B is 118°. Find interior angle A.
practice.solution: Interior B=180−118=62°. Angle C is also 62°, so angle A=180−124=56°.

practice.prompt: Equal sides are (3x+2) cm and (5x−20) cm; base is 24 cm. Find the perimeter.
practice.solution: 3x+2=5x−20 gives x=11. Each leg is 35 cm; perimeter=35+35+24=94 cm.

practice.prompt: Vertex is (4x+10)° and each base angle is (2x+5)°. Find exterior angle at a base vertex.
practice.solution: 4x+10+2(2x+5)=180 gives x=20. Base angle=45°, so exterior=180−45=135°.

test.prompt: Vertex angle is 54°. Find either base angle.
Each base angle is 41°. Find the vertex angle.
Equal legs are (4x+3) cm and (6x−15) cm, base 20 cm. Find perimeter.
test.solution: 4x+3=6x−15 gives x=9. Each leg=39 cm, so perimeter=39+39+20=98 cm.

test.prompt: Vertex is (2x+20)° and each base angle is (3x+4)°. Find x.
Exterior angle at vertex is (6x+10)°, each base angle (2x+15)°. Find interior vertex angle.
test.solution: 6x+10=2(2x+15) gives x=10. Exterior is 70°, so interior vertex=180−70=110°.
